stops.note: a pitchfork; a defeated Roman army was forced under a yoke at the Caudine Forks (Furculae Caudinae) in 321 BC
a farm pitchfork, reinforced later by Norman French forque
table forks reached England late: Thomas Coryat described Italians eating with them in his Crudities (1611) and was mocked for copying them

current_meaning: a pronged utensil for eating or a pronged farm tool
